parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim, and the counterexample is correct. With distinct atoms c, a_i, b_j, every F_i = {c, a_i, b_1,...,b_{i-1}} contains c, so the family is pairwise intersecting and has the size-2 member F_1. Each B_n = {a_1,...,a_n, b_n} meets every F_i (a_i for i<=n; b_n lies in F_i for i>n), and is minimal: deleting a_k leaves F_k unmet, deleting b_n leaves F_{n+1} unmet; the B_n are distinct. So there are infinitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals, refuting the blocker fact. Moreover, any finite family B_1,...,B_s satisfying the finite-transversal lemma must include every minimal transversal (if M is minimal and B_j is a transversal with B_j ⊆ M, then B_j = M), so the lemma itself is false. It is the write-up's only source of finiteness; no alternative is proved elsewhere. Fatal.
